subject: general
question: The Chuar Rebellion, which emerged as a culmination of the economic grievances of ordinary peasants and hereditary workers, reached its peak during which of the following years?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1798-99**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The** Chuar Rebellion** was a series of uprisings by the tribal communities, primarily the **Chuar and Bhumij tribes**, in Bengal and Bihar against British colonial rule.
 
• The rebellion occurred due to severe **economic grievances**, including the imposition of heavy land revenue and exploitation by British officials.
 
• The peak of the Chuar rebellion was witnessed during the years **1798-99**, when widespread unrest impacted regions such as **Midnapore and Jungle Mahal.**
 
• British policies, such as the Permanent Settlement Act of 1793, further alienated the tribal population by depriving them of their traditional rights to land and forest resources.
 
• The rebellion was ultimately suppressed through military interventions and administrative measures by the British.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Permanent Settlement Act (1793):**

 
 
• Implemented by Lord Cornwallis, this act introduced the zamindari system of land revenue collection.
 
• It fixed the revenue payable by zamindars permanently, depriving the tribal communities of their customary land rights.
 
 
 
• **Jungle Mahal:**
 
 
• A region in Bengal that included parts of present-day West Bengal, Odisha, and Jharkhand.
 
• The area was historically inhabited by tribal communities such as the Bhumij and Chuar.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Uprisings:**
 
 
• In the 18th and 19th centuries, several tribal rebellions occurred due to British exploitation, including the **Santhal Rebellion (1855-56)** and the **Kol Rebellion (1831-32).**
 
• These uprisings highlighted the socio-economic struggles faced by tribal populations under colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Colonial Economic Policies:**
 
 
• British colonial policies disrupted the traditional tribal economy, leading to widespread poverty and dispossession.
 
• Heavy land taxes and restrictions on forest use exacerbated the grievances of tribal communities.
